question: Which of the following shortcut keys is used to switch between open applications in Windows?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Alt + Tab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Alt + Tab** shortcut key is used to switch between open applications in the **Windows operating system**. This feature is called **Task Switching**.
 
• By pressing and holding the **Alt** key and then pressing the **Tab** key, users can cycle through the thumbnails of all currently open applications to quickly choose the desired one.
 
• This functionality enhances **productivity** by allowing users to navigate between multiple programs and windows efficiently, without using a mouse.
 
• The **Alt + Tab** feature has been part of Microsoft Windows since its early versions and is widely recognized as a core keyboard shortcut for multitasking.
 
• When users hold the **Alt key** and repeatedly press **Tab**, they can scroll through the list of running applications until the desired window is highlighted, and releasing the keys will bring that window to the foreground.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alt + Ins:**

 
 
• This shortcut is not used for switching between applications in Windows. Instead, it is used in specific software or environments, such as virtual machine consoles, to insert system commands or perform special operations.
 
• It has limited use and is not a widely recognized shortcut for multitasking.
 
 
 
• **Alt + F4:**
 
 
• This shortcut is used for closing the currently active window or application in Windows.
 
• It is a quick method to exit programs or shut down the system when no application windows are open.
 
 
 
• **Alt + Del:**
 
 
• This shortcut is not associated with switching between applications. It is used in specific contexts, such as deleting files or accessing advanced menus in some software environments.
 
• It does not serve the purpose of multitasking or task switching.
 
 
 
• **Windows Task View:**
 
 
• Introduced in Windows 10, Task View is another multitasking tool that allows users to view all open applications and virtual desktops.
 
• It can be accessed by pressing **Win + Tab**, which provides a more visual and detailed representation of open windows compared to Alt + Tab.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Multitasking:**

 
 
• Keyboard shortcuts like **Alt + Tab** are essential for **multitasking**, enabling users to manage multiple applications quickly and efficiently.
 
• Such shortcuts improve **workflow**, saving time and reducing reliance on mouse navigation.
 
 
 
• **Accessibility:**
 
 
• These shortcuts are particularly beneficial for users with physical limitations, providing an efficient way to navigate the system without requiring extensive mouse movement.
 
• They are integral to the **Windows accessibility features**.
 
 
 
• **Consistency Across Versions:**
 
 
• The **Alt + Tab** shortcut has remained consistent across different versions of Windows, making it a dependable tool for users familiar with the system.
 
• Its functionality has been enhanced in newer versions of Windows, offering smoother transitions and better visual representation of open applications.
